test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: On simple interest a certain sum becomes 160% of itself in 5 years at a certain rate of interest per annum. In how many years will the sum double itself under the same rate of interest?
solution:
**Given:**

Time = 5 years

Sum become 160% of itself after 5 years

**Concept used:**

S.I = Ptr/100

Here,

P = Principal or sum

r = rate

t = time

**Calculation:**

Let the sum be 100P and rate of interest be r

So, after the amount = 100P × 160%

⇒ 160P

So, interest in 5 years = 160P - 100P

⇒ 60P

Now,

60P = (100P × 5 × r)/100

⇒ 60P = 5Pr

⇒ 5r = 60

⇒ r = 60/5 = 12

So, rate = 12%

Now,

Double of sum = 200P

So, interest = 200P - 100P 

⇒ 100P

Now,

Let time for the sum to become double of itself be t

So,

100P = (100P × t × 12)/100

⇒ 100P = 12Pt

⇒ 12t = 100

⇒ t = 100/12

⇒ t = 8(1)/(3)

So, the required time is 8(1)/(3)

**∴ In 8(1)/(3) years will the sum double itself under the same rate of interest.**
